chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu 'Umarah al-Munshid, who said:

Whenever al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) was mentioned in the presence of Abu 'Abdillah, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), during the day, Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) would not be seen smiling on that day until nightfall.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Husayn ibn Ali, the third Shia Imam

ai.seo_question: What was the reaction of Imam al-Sadiq when Imam al-Husayn was mentioned?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the profound affective bond between Imam al-Sadiq and his grandfather, illustrating how the memory of Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom evoked a sustained state of solemn contemplation throughout the day. In Shia tradition, this consistent lack of smiling serves as a spiritual indicator of deep grief (*huzn*) and reverence, linking the Imam’s personal emotional response to the broader communal practice of mourning (*mawt*). It highlights that remembrance of the Ahl al-Bayt is not merely intellectual but deeply experiential, shaping the spiritual demeanor of the Imams.
